newsitem.title: USA: US spot resid prices extends loss amid weaker gas.
newsitem.headline: US spot resid prices extends loss amid weaker gas.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices extended their recent losses in line with weaker natural gas prices and forecast of mild weather across the eastern U.S. for the remainder of February.
"There's not a lot of good news for resid. Natgas is weaker," said an East Coast physical trader.
NYMEX March Henry Hub natural gas futures settled down 9.1 cents at $1.999 per million British thermal units.
New York Harbor physical one percent softened to $16.38 a barrel from Wednesday's $16.50 a barrel area, with March paper slipping to $16.00-15 from $16.35-50 yesterday, traders said.
A rebound in crude futures failed to offset bearish sentiment overhanging the key New York harbor and U.S. Gulf markets. NYMEX March crude ended up 16 cents at $22.02 a barrel.
NYH 0.3 percent high pour edged down to $18.00-25, off 25 cents after a deal heard done at $17.90 late Wednesday.
All other NYH sulphur grades were pegged lower amid lackluster utility and bunker demand, market sources said.
USG prices fell another quarter with aggressive offers of mid- and high-sulphur supplies. One percent grade was pegged at $15.00-25 and three percent at $12.25-50.
Expected startup of two USG coker units later this week may limit further downside in HSFO prices, traders said.
New York city gate gas prices dropped 30 cents to $2.75-2.80/mmBtu compared with a NYH one percent resid equivalent of $2.60/mmBtu.
